pages.note: The first page of the book's ROMAN section and the opening of the sutta. A centred title Mahasamayasutta at the head, then seventeen lines of PROSE — ink measured x 280-1860 with no internal gutter, and hanging-indent continuations starting at x 400, which is how the wrapped lines were told from new ones. Two TWO-COLUMN gatha rows at the foot, gutters measured at x 878-992 and x 800-898, read ACROSS. The sheet runs out and the sutta carries on to page 318.

working_notes.units: Twenty-two. Three prose paragraphs (1-6, 7-11, 12-17), a two-column gatha (18-19), one prose line (20) and a second gatha (21-22). The chant's own layout is 'prose' because it opens and mostly runs as prose; the two gatha groups override with para_layout 'lines'.

chants.title_english: The Discourse on the Great Assembly

verses.pali_roman: Evaṃ me sutaṃ:
verses.english: Thus have I heard:

verses.pali_roman: Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā
verses.english: At one time the Blessed One

verses.pali_roman: sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ mahāvane
verses.english: was dwelling among the Sakyans, at Kapilavatthu in the Great Wood,

verses.pali_roman: mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi.
verses.english: together with a great community of bhikkhus, five hundred bhikkhus, all of them arahants.

verses.pali_roman: Dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca.
verses.english: And from ten world-systems the deities had for the most part gathered to see the Blessed One and the community of bhikkhus.

verses.pali_roman: Atha kho catunnaṃ suddhāvāsakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ etadahosi:
verses.english: Then it occurred to four deities of the Pure Abodes:

verses.pali_roman: “Ayaṃ kho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ mahāvane
verses.english: “This Blessed One is dwelling among the Sakyans, at Kapilavatthu in the Great Wood,

verses.pali_roman: mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi
verses.english: together with a great community of bhikkhus, five hundred bhikkhus, all of them arahants,

verses.pali_roman: dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca.
verses.english: and from ten world-systems the deities have for the most part gathered to see the Blessed One and the community of bhikkhus.

verses.pali_roman: Yannūna mayampi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkameyyāma.
verses.english: What if we too were to approach the Blessed One,

verses.pali_roman: Upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike paccekagāthā bhāseyyāmā”ti.
verses.english: and having approached, each speak a verse in his presence?”

verses.pali_roman: Atha kho tā devatā
verses.english: Then those deities —

verses.pali_roman: seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya,
verses.english: just as a strong man might extend his bent arm,

verses.pali_roman: pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya,
verses.english: or bend his extended arm —

verses.pali_roman: evameva suddhāvāsesu devesu antarahitā bhagavato purato pāturahaṃsu.
verses.english: just so vanished from among the deities of the Pure Abodes and appeared before the Blessed One.

verses.pali_roman: Atha kho tā devatā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu.
verses.english: Then those deities paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side.

verses.pali_roman: Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi:
verses.english: Standing to one side, one deity spoke this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

verses.pali_roman: “Mahā samayo pavanasmiṃ. Devakāyā samāgatā:
verses.english: “A great assembly in the woodland: the hosts of devas have come together;

verses.pali_roman: ‘Āgatamha imaṃ dhammasamayaṃ dakkhitāye v’aparājitasaṅghan’ti”.
verses.english: ‘we have come to this assembly of the Dhamma, to see the invincible Saṅgha’.”

verses.pali_roman: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi:
verses.english: Then another deity spoke this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

verses.pali_roman: “Tatra bhikkhavo samādahaṃsu cittamattano ujuka-makaṃsu.
verses.english: “There the bhikkhus are composed; they have made their own minds straight.

verses.pali_roman: Sārathīva nettāni gahetvā indriyāni rakkhanti paṇḍitā”ti.
verses.english: Like a charioteer holding the reins, the wise ones guard their faculties.”

vocabulary.meaning: the great assembly or great gathering — the coming together of devas from ten world-systems that gives the sutta its name
the Pure Abodes, the five highest Brahma worlds where non-returners are reborn. The four devas who open the sutta come from there
a verse spoken each on his own — one deity, one verse, which is the shape the whole opening takes
woodland, forest. Here the Mahavana at Kapilavatthu

checks.issue: THE BOOK PRINTS THIS SECTION IN ROMAN PALI WITH NO THAI SCRIPT — the first page in the whole book to do so. Every verse therefore has an EMPTY pali and carries its text in pali_roman, and paiboon is empty because Paiboon+ romanises the Thai and there is no Thai. Read at 3x across the whole sheet: no Thai character appears anywhere on it, title included. This needed a template change before the page could render — book mode hid pali_roman, so the sheet would have come out blank.

THE SAME SUTTA IS ALREADY IN THE BOOK IN THAI SCRIPT. The book's own contents lists mahasamayasuttam at page 175, with its own bot khat above it. So the book prints this sutta TWICE, in two scripts, in two places. This entry is the ROMAN printing and is deliberately a SEPARATE chant with the id suffixed -roman, so that page 175 can be entered later without one page overwriting the other's text. Whether the two should eventually be joined is Josh's call; nothing here forecloses it.
Evam me sutam: is set in BOLD, and so is Maha samayo pavanasmim at verse 18. The bold marks where a unit begins. The app has no bold layer, so this is recorded rather than reproduced.

The page prints a DOUBLE SPACE inside 'pasaritam va baham  saminjeyya' — two clear spaces between baham and saminjeyya at 5x, where every other gap on the line is single. Read as compositor's spacing and normalised to one space; the words themselves are not in doubt.

TWO COLUMNS, gutter measured at x 878-992 by profiling the ink across the row rather than judging it by eye. Verse 18 reads ACROSS: Maha samayo pavanasmim. in the left column, Devakaya samagata: in the right.

TWO COLUMNS again, gutter measured at x 800-898 — a different measure from verse 18's on the same sheet, so each gatha block was profiled separately rather than one measurement assumed for the whole page.

batch_status.paiboon_scan: clean, and trivially so. The page prints no Thai, so every paiboon is empty and there is no Paiboon+ anywhere in the batch — no title_roman either, because the contents does not list this printing. Scanned every romanised slot for kh, th, ph and ng: zero hits.
batch_status.pali_untouched: Confirmed, with the sense inverted for this page. There is no Thai-script pali to leave untouched — every pali value is empty by design — and every pali_roman is the page's own roman text copied letter for letter, diacritics included: n with dot below in pavanasmim and saminjitam, m with dot below throughout, a-macron and i-macron as set. No pali_roman has been re-spelled towards the Thai-script conventions used elsewhere in the book.
batch_status.page_scan: agrees. One row for one page covering verses 1-22, which is the whole entry. Verse 1 carries the page key and starts the chant. No verse is orphaned and none is claimed twice. No page blocks and no footnotes on this sheet.
batch_status.notes: A hand is at the foot of the photograph and covers no text — the last line of ink ends at y 2510 and the fingers begin below y 2600, with clear paper between. Three findings. (1) THE ROMAN SECTION IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF PAGE and needed a template fix before it could render at all — see the first check. (2) THE SUTTA IS IN THE BOOK TWICE, here in roman and at page 175 in Thai script, which means the back of the book may be a roman reprint of material already listed in the contents rather than new chants. Worth settling before the rest of the roman section goes in. (3) Layout was MEASURED: prose ink x 280-1860 with no gutter, hanging indents at x 400, and the two gatha gutters at x 878-992 and x 800-898, each profiled on its own row band.
